summary: Peter von Köppen worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the National University of Kharkiv (c. 1810–1814) and the University of Tübingen (c. 1822–1824), later holding a post at the Ministry of State Property (c. 1837–1860).

Petr Sgall was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Charles University from c. 1945 to 1949, completing his doctorate under Vincenc Lesný, and later served on the faculty at Charles University from c. 1953 to 1995.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Heinz Bechert (c. 1982–1990). She held posts at the University of Göttingen (c. 1988–2002), Mainz Academy (c. 2003), and the Pali Text Society (c. 2010).

Petra Maurer is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has held posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences, the University of Munich, IKGF Erlangen (2017), and the Göttingen Academy.

id: P:Petrus Abraham Samuel van Limburg Brouwer
summary: Petrus Abraham Samuel van Limburg Brouwer was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Groningen from 1844 to 1850, receiving a Dr.juris degree, and held a research post at the Nationaal Archief in 1865.

Phakchok Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under several traditional teachers, earned a Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute (c. 1998–2005), and became Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling c. 2000.
Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, studying under supervisors Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Phanit Jetjiravat is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the academic advisement of Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a sinologist and historian educated at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown. He held faculty posts at the University of Chicago (1963–1978) and Harvard University from 1978, also directing the Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies (1980–1986).

Philip A. Mellor is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989. As of 2010, he held a professorship and head of school post at the University of Leeds.
Philip Anderson was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge (c. 1834–1838) and served as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Philip Boas Yampolsky worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University and under Yoshitaka Iriya, later serving as an adjunct associate professor and librarian at Columbia (1968–1996) and chairing the Numata Center (1991–1996).

Philip C. Almond is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Adelaide (1975–1980) and held a post at the University of Queensland beginning in 1982, where he is emeritus professor.

Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from c. 1991 to 1996. Around 2008, he became Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig.

Philip Deslippe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Connecticut, University of Iowa, and UC Santa Barbara, where he was attested as a teaching associate in 2020.

Philip Kapleau was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Soen Nakagawa, Sogaku Harada, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and the Chapin Mill Retreat Center (1996).

Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He taught at Brown University (c. 1971–1985), became O'Brien Professor at Notre Dame in 1985, and was APA President (1994–1995).

Philip Lutgendorf is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (c. 1971–1987). He joined the University of Iowa faculty in 1985 and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010–2018).

Philip Novak is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Notre Dame (c. 1968–1972) and Syracuse University, and began teaching at Dominican University of California around 1980.

Philip Stanley Rawson was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. Educated at Oxford, the Courtauld Institute, and SOAS, he taught at the Royal College of Art (c. 1975–1981) and served as dean at the University of London (c. 1981–1984).
